data.name: Govardhan
data.gender_notes: Govardhan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Govardhan is a name derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Govardhana’, which means ‘governing all’. In Hindu mythology, Lord Krishna, who is often depicted as Govardhan, is believed to have lifted the hill Govardhana to protect the people of Vrindavan from Indra's wrath. Thus, Govardhan is a name symbolizing protection and governance.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that evokes the divine protector within.
data.etymology: Govardhan belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Protector of the Earth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Govardhan total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Govardhan holds significant cultural importance in Hinduism, as it is widely associated with Lord Krishna, a deity revered by Hindus and worshipped across India and beyond. The name is often invoked during religious ceremonies, and it is common to see images and statues of Lord Krishna as Govardhana.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Govardhan is believed to represent the all-pervading consciousness of God, who governs and protects all beings. The name also symbolizes the power of love and devotion, as Lord Krishna's actions to protect the people of Vrindavan illustrate the depth of his love and care for his devotees. Additionally, the name Govardhan is associated with the qualities of compassion, generosity, and purity, making it a powerful representation of the divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Govardhan represents the divine cow-god Krishna, whose name signifies one who gives joy (Gov) and removes suffering (Vardhan). It also symbolizes the infinite nourisher and protector of all beings.

historical_references.reference: According to Hindu mythology, Lord Krishna is depicted as having grown up in the village of Gokula, near Mathura. The village was protected by the hill named Govardhana. When the demon king Kamsa attacked the village, Lord Krishna, in his childhood, lifted the hill Govardhana on his little finger and held it above his head as an umbrella to protect the village from the demon's attacks.

Another reference to the name Govardhana comes from the epic Mahabharata. In this text, there is a mention of a Yaksha named Govardhana, who was the guardian of the cowherd settlement of Vraja. He was the father of the cowherd king, Ugrasena, and was also known as the presiding deity of the kingdom.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Govardhan' is popularly used in modern Hindu culture, particularly in the context of Deity worship. Govardhan is the name of a form of Lord Krishna, who is often depicted as a cowherd boy playing with cattle in Vrindavan. The name is also synonymous with the idea of 'Govardhana Puja', a ritualistic event where the deity is symbolically represented by an idol made of clay and decorated with a variety of offerings. This tradition is celebrated widely during the Hindu festival of Diwali and other religious occasions. The name 'Govardhan' is also associated with vegetarianism and the concept of 'ahimsa' or non-violence, as Lord Krishna himself is believed to be a vegetarian. The name can be seen frequently on social media platforms like Instagram, where devotees post pictures of their beautifully decorated Govardhan idols and the offerings made to them. YouTube is another platform where one can find numerous videos on the making and decoration of Govardhan idols, as well as the actual Govardhan Puja ceremony itself. Finally, on Reddit, there are numerous threads dedicated to discussions about the symbolism and significance of Govardhan in Hinduism, as well as personal experiences and stories related to the practice of Govardhan Puja.
